The great Pullman was whirling onward with such dignity of motion that a glance from the window seemed simply to prove that the plains of Texas were pouring eastward. <break time="0.8s" /> A newly married pair had boarded this coach at San Antonio, and the mans face was reddened from many days in the wind and sun. <break time="0.8s" /> Wearing new black clothes, he kept moving his brick colored hands in a self conscious way, and from time to time he looked down respectfully at his attire. <break time="0.8s" /> The bride was not pretty, nor was she very young, and she wore a dress of blue cashmere with small touches of velvet and many steel buttons. <break time="0.8s" /> She kept turning her head to look at her stiff, high puffed sleeves, and it was quite apparent that she had cooked, and expected to cook, dutifully. <break time="0.8s" /> Have you ever been in a parlor car before, he asked, smiling with delight, and she answered shyly that she never had. <break time="0.8s" /> He told her proudly that they would go forward to the diner later and get a big lay out, the finest meal in the world, for a dollar. <break time="0.8s" /> To the minds of the pair, the shining coach reflected the glory of their marriage that morning in San Antonio, though the porter quietly looked down on them.
